questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)-2xy,\,y(0)=-2
$$

The trapezoidal method is applied with step size $Δx=3.$ Find the general formula for the new $y$ value, ${y}_{\text{new}},$ in terms of the current values $x$ and $y,$ and the new value ${x}_{\text{new}}.$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In this example, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)-2xy+(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}}+1)-2{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}}+1)-2xy)-3{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{3}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}}+1)-2xy)-3{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{3}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}}+1)-2xy+\frac{2}{3}y)-3{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}}+3{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{3}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}}+1)-2xy+\frac{2}{3}y) \\ {y}_{\text{new}}(1+3{x}_{\text{new}}) & =\frac{3}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}}+1)-2xy+\frac{2}{3}y) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}}+1)-6xy+2y}{2+6{x}_{\text{new}}}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{y}^{′}={e}^{x}-3xy,\,y(-2)=3
$$

The trapezoidal method is applied with step size $Δx=1.$ Find the general formula for the new $y$ value, ${y}_{\text{new}},$ in terms of the current values $x$ and $y,$ and the new value ${x}_{\text{new}}.$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In this example, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}-3xy+({e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}-3{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}-3xy)-\frac{3}{2}{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}-3xy)-\frac{3}{2}{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}-3xy+2y)-\frac{3}{2}{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}}+\frac{3}{2}{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}-3xy+2y) \\ \frac{1}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}(2+3{x}_{\text{new}}) & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}-3xy+2y) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{{e}^{x}+{e}^{{x}_{\text{new}}}-3xy+2y}{2+3{x}_{\text{new}}}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=-x+3y,\,y(0)=2
$$

The trapezoidal method is applied with step size $Δx=1.$ Find the general formula for the new $y$ value, ${y}_{\text{new}},$ in terms of the current values $x$ and $y,$ and the new value ${x}_{\text{new}}.$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In this example, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-x+3y+(-{x}_{\text{new}}+3{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-x-{x}_{\text{new}}+3y)+\frac{3}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{2}(-x-{x}_{\text{new}}+3y)+\frac{3}{2}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{2}(-x-{x}_{\text{new}}+5y)+\frac{3}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{2}(-x-{x}_{\text{new}}+5y) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =x+{x}_{\text{new}}-5y\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}={e}^{2x}+{x}^{2}y,\,y(0)=1
$$

The trapezoidal method is applied with step size $Δx=2.$ Find the general formula for the new $y$ value, ${y}_{\text{new}},$ in terms of the current values $x$ and $y,$ and the new value ${x}_{\text{new}}.$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In this example, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{2x}+{x}^{2}y+({e}^{2{x}_{\text{new}}}+{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot 2 \\  & ={e}^{2x}+{e}^{2{x}_{\text{new}}}+{x}^{2}y+{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+{e}^{2x}+{e}^{2{x}_{\text{new}}}+{x}^{2}y+{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & ={e}^{2x}+{e}^{2{x}_{\text{new}}}+({x}^{2}+1)y+{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}}-{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}{y}_{\text{new}} & ={e}^{2x}+{e}^{2{x}_{\text{new}}}+({x}^{2}+1)y \\ {y}_{\text{new}}(1-{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}) & ={e}^{2x}+{e}^{2{x}_{\text{new}}}+({x}^{2}+1)y \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{{e}^{2x}+{e}^{2{x}_{\text{new}}}+({x}^{2}+1)y}{1-{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=4x-5y,\,y(-2)=1
$$

The trapezoidal method is applied with step size $Δx=5.$ Find the general formula for the new $y$ value, ${y}_{\text{new}},$ in terms of the current values $x$ and $y,$ and the new value ${x}_{\text{new}}.$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In this example, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4x-5y+(4{x}_{\text{new}}-5{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot 5 \\  & =\frac{5}{2}(4x+4{x}_{\text{new}}-5y)-\frac{25}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{5}{2}(4x+4{x}_{\text{new}}-5y)-\frac{25}{2}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{5}{2}\,(4x+4{x}_{\text{new}}-\frac{23}{5}y)-\frac{25}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{27}{2}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{5}{2}\,(4x+4{x}_{\text{new}}-\frac{23}{5}y) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{5}{27}\,(4x+4{x}_{\text{new}}-\frac{23}{5}y) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{27}(20x+20{x}_{\text{new}}-23y)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=y({x}^{2}+1),\,y(-1)=\frac{11}{3}
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step to approximate $y\,(-\frac{1}{2}),$ rounded to two decimal places.

$$
y\,(-\frac{1}{2})≈{{field-1}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=-\frac{1}{2},$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=-\frac{1}{2}-(-1)=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(y({x}^{2}+1)+{y}_{\text{new}}(({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}+1))\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}y({x}^{2}+1)+\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}(({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{4}y({x}^{2}+1)+\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}(({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}+1) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{4}y({x}^{2}+5)+\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}+\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}-\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}({x}_{\text{new}})^{2} & =\frac{1}{4}y({x}^{2}+5) \\ \frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}(3-({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}) & =\frac{1}{4}y({x}^{2}+5) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{y({x}^{2}+5)}{3-({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=-1+\frac{1}{2}=-\frac{1}{2}.$ Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{y({x}^{2}+5)}{3-({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{11}{3}((-1)^{2}+5)}{3-{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{22}{(\frac{11}{4})} \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y\,(-\frac{1}{2})≈8.00.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=y(3\sqrt{x}+2),\,y(0)=2
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step to approximate $y(1),$ rounded to two decimal places.

$$
y(1)≈{{field-1}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=1,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=1-0=1.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(y(3\sqrt{x}+2)+{y}_{\text{new}}(3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}+2))\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,y(3\sqrt{x}+2)+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}+2).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{2}\,y(3\sqrt{x}+2)+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}+2) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{2}y(3\sqrt{x}+4)+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}+2)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}}-\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}+2) & =\frac{1}{2}y(3\sqrt{x}+4) \\ \frac{1}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}(-3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}) & =\frac{1}{2}y(3\sqrt{x}+4) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =-\frac{y(3\sqrt{x}+4)}{3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=0+1=1.$ Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =-\frac{y(3\sqrt{x}+4)}{3\sqrt{{x}_{\text{new}}}} \\  & =-\frac{2(3\sqrt{0}+4)}{3\sqrt{1}} \\  & =-\frac{8}{3} \\  & ≈-2.67.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y(1)≈-2.67.$

$$
{y}^{′}=y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1),\,y(1)=1
$$

$$

$$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$

$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=2,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=2-1=1.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)+{y}_{\text{new}}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})+1))\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})+1).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{2}\,y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})+1) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{2}y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+3)+\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}}-\frac{1}{2}\,{y}_{\text{new}}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})+1) & =\frac{1}{2}y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+3) \\ \frac{1}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}(1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})) & =\frac{1}{2}y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+3) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+3)}{1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=1+1=2.$ Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{y(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+3)}{1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{\text{new}})} \\  & =\frac{1(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+3)}{1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)} \\  & =\frac{3}{1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)} \\  & ≈-7.77.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y(2)≈-7.77.$

Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=-x+4y,\,y(1)=0
$$

$$

$$

For an initial value problem

$$

$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=3,$ we will use a step size of

$$

$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-x+4y+(-{x}_{\text{new}}+4{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot 2 \\  & =-x-{x}_{\text{new}}+4y+4{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y-x-{x}_{\text{new}}+4y+4{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =-x-{x}_{\text{new}}+5y+4{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{y}_{\text{new}} & =-x-{x}_{\text{new}}+5y \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{3}(x+{x}_{\text{new}}-5y)\end{aligned}

$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
y' = 3x^2 - 2y, \qquad y(3) = -1
$$

The trapezoidal method is applied with step size $\Delta x = 4.$ Find the general formula for the new $y$ value, $y_\text{new},$ in terms of the current values $x$ and $y,$ and the new value $x_\text{new}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
y' = f(x,y), \qquad y(a) = c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $\Delta x$ is given by

$$
\Delta y = \dfrac12(y' + y'_\text{new}) \cdot \Delta x,
$$

with $y'_\text{new} = f(x_\text{new}, y_\text{new})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In this example, $\Delta y$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3{x}^{2}-2y+(3({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-2{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot 4 \\  & =6{x}^{2}+6{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}-4y-4{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into $y_\text{new} = y + \Delta y{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+6{x}^{2}+6{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}-4y-4{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =6{x}^{2}+6({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-3y-4{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for the general formula for $y_\text{new}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}5{y}_{\text{new}} & =6{x}^{2}+6({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-3y \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{5}(6{x}^{2}+6({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-3y)\end{aligned}
$$

For an initial value problem

$$

$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $\Delta x$ is given by

$$

$$

with $y'_\text{new} = f(x_\text{new}, y_\text{new})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=\dfrac43,$ we will use a step size of

$$
\Delta x = \dfrac43 - 1 = \dfrac13.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $\Delta y$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2x-y+(2{x}_{\text{new}}-{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(2x-y+2{x}_{\text{new}}-{y}_{\text{new}}) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(2x-y+2{x}_{\text{new}})-\frac{1}{6}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into $y_\text{new} = y + \Delta y{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{6}(2x-y+2{x}_{\text{new}})-\frac{1}{6}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{6}(2x+2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y)-\frac{1}{6}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for $y_\text{new}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{6}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{6}(2x+2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{7}(2x+2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is $x_\text{new} = 1 + \dfrac13 = \dfrac43.$ Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{7}(2x+2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}(2\cdot 1+2\cdot \frac{4}{3}+5\cdot 0) \\  & =\frac{2}{3} \\  & ≈0.67.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y\!\left(\dfrac43\right) \approx 0.67.$

\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{3}(4x+4{x}_{\text{new}}+y) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(4\cdot 1+4\cdot 2+1.33) \\  & ≈4.44.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
y(1) \approx 1.33,
\qquad
y(2) \approx 4.44.
$$
